title: Air-fryer whole chicken
subtitle: A full roast chicken in the air fryer in under an hour.
excerpt: A whole chicken under 1.5 kg cooks beautifully in the air fryer: skin blistered and golden, meat moist through to the bone. No basting, no large oven. Ready in about 55 minutes. Serves four.
sourceNotes: Roast chicken is a staple of British and French home cooking. The air fryer replicates the convection-oven effect at a smaller scale: circulating hot air crisps the skin while keeping the breast meat from drying out. The technique has been widely adopted since air fryers became mainstream kitchen appliances in the 2010s.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Rub the chicken with the spiced butter up to 24 hours ahead and keep it uncovered in the fridge. The skin dries out further and crisps better.

content.text: A whole chicken under 1.5 kg fits most standard air fryers and cooks in about 55 minutes at 180°C, giving properly golden skin and meat that comes cleanly off the bone. The key is choosing the right-sized bird: anything much over 1.5 kg won't fit or cook evenly. Pat it completely dry before seasoning; wet skin steams rather than crisps.
Check the internal temperature with a probe thermometer: 75°C at the thickest part of the thigh, not touching bone. Rest for ten minutes before carving ,  the juices settle and the meat stays moist.

Mix {{olive-oil}} of olive oil with {{sea-salt-flakes}} of flaked salt, {{paprika-smoked}} of smoked paprika, {{garlic-powder}} of garlic powder, and {{paprika-sweet}} of sweet paprika to form a paste. Pat the {{chicken-whole}} chicken completely dry inside and out with paper towels. Rub the paste all over the skin, getting into the crevices between the legs and body. Tuck the wing tips under the bird. If using, press {{lemon}} halved lemon into the cavity.

Preheat the air fryer to 180°C for 3 minutes. Place the chicken breast-side down in the basket. Cook at 180°C for 30 minutes. Flip the chicken breast-side up and cook for a further 20-25 minutes, until the skin is deep golden and a probe thermometer reads 75°C at the thickest part of the thigh. Rest on a board for 10 minutes before carving.

items.symptom: Skin pale and soft, not golden
items.cause: Bird not dried before seasoning, or basket too cold at the start.
items.fix: Pat dry thoroughly. Preheat the air fryer before adding the chicken.

items.symptom: Breast meat dry before thighs are cooked
items.fix: Always start breast-side down. This shields the breast from direct heat and allows the thighs to cook faster from below.

items.symptom: Bird too large to fit or cook unevenly
items.fix: Use a spatchcocked chicken for larger birds. Remove the backbone and flatten the bird before air-frying.

items.symptom: Temperature reads low but skin is very dark
items.cause: Probe touching bone rather than meat.
items.fix: Insert the thermometer into the thickest part of the thigh without touching the bone. The reading should be 75°C.

content.text: Whole air-fryer chicken is the weeknight roast for households without time or inclination to heat a large oven. The result is closer to a rotisserie chicken than a traditional Sunday roast: crisp skin, moist meat, nothing basted. Good with roast potatoes cooked in a second round in the same basket, or with a simple green salad.
